 No boos, only silence at Ball Arena as Warriors clobber Nuggets 
 Denver lost Nikola Jokic’s minutes by 16 points as Golden State pulled away in the second half of another deflating home game

 Aaron Gordon (32) of the Denver Nuggets walks to the bench during the third quarter against the Golden State Warriors at Ball Arena in Denver, Colorado on Monday, October 26, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) 
 By Bennett Durando | bdurando@denverpost.com | The Denver Post PUBLISHED: October 26, 2026 at 10:48 PM MDT | UPDATED: October 27, 2026 at 9:21 AM MDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Nuggets fans were reprimanded by Nikola Jokic himself for booing the team Saturday. They stewed in uncomfortable silence instead on Monday as Jokic and company slowly dug another 20-point deficit against the winless Golden State Warriors.
 They are winless no more, after running the Nuggets out of their own deflated gym. The final score: 134-114. The record in Denver: 1-2, the lone win marked by Denver’s jeers that preceded a desperate 23-point comeback. Nuggets fans now get a week off as the team embarks on a two-game road trip to New Orleans and Phoenix.
 The Nuggets never led after halftime. They were out-rebounded 50-36, giving up 23 second-chance points. They were out-attempted 44-29 from 3-point range. They made 34.5% of theirs, including a 1-for-6 night from Nikola Jokic that brought him to a 5-for-23 clip three games into the season; their visitors knocked down 50% of their 3s.
 Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg led the Warriors with 31 points and 12 rebounds, accounting for 12 of their 20 free throws. Steph Curry scored 21 of his 24 points in the second half, never missing a shot. Brandin Podziemski added 18 points, seven boards and five assists with a plus-33 to boot.
 DeMar DeRozan led Denver with 21 points off the bench. Jokic and Murray scored 19 each, but the Nuggets lost Jokic’s minutes by 16. Murray tried to stir another late comeback to no avail. Aaron Gordon struggled to make his presence felt at either end for the second consecutive game. He was ejected with 8:34 remaining and a 2-for-10 shooting line after he got in the referees’ ears for an illegal screen that was called against Christian Braun.
 Jamal Murray (27) of the Denver Nuggets passes as Draymond Green (23) and De’anthony Melton (8) of the Golden State Warriors defend during the third quarter at Ball Arena in Denver, Colorado on Monday, October 26, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) 
 Denver remained without Cam Johnson (ankle), Spencer Jones (hamstring), Alpha Diallo (wrist) and Julian Strawther (knee). Rookie Bryce Hopkins continued to start at small forward, and second-year coach David Adelman used a nine-man rotation that decreased to eight in the second half with Tyus Jones’ night ending at eight minutes.

 The Nuggets started playing with fire again in the second quarter, when a rest for Jokic coincided with a stint on the court for Curry. Even though he wasn’t scoring, his gravity was enough to get the wheels in motion for Denver’s help defense. Georges Niang buried a pair of 3s, and Golden State strung together a 13-4 run to go up by five. Denver temporarily steadied the ship with an 8-0 run out of a timeout, but the Warriors kept coming.
 Backup center Al Horford was able to stretch out the defense, as he did last season in a win over Denver. Lendeborg drove at Jokic relentlessly. Podziemski made plays on and off the ball. Golden State went into halftime with a four-point edge — and then Curry woke up. The legendary shooter eagerly took the torch from his teammates. He scurried up the floor for a layup on the first possession of the half, then amassed 17 points on 6-for-6 shooting over the next eight minutes.
 His team raced to an 80-65 lead with 6:44 left in the frame. Like most of last Saturday, the Nuggets couldn’t show enough defensive resistance to maintain momentum whenever they briefly captured it. A quick 5-0 run by DeRozan went nowhere. A rookie-to-rookie alley-oop that resulted in Trevon Brazile cutting the gap to 89-82 went nowhere. It was back up to 16 by the end of the third.
